answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making each extra identity more expensive: the first identity is nearly free, but every additional identity tied to the same device, payment rail, or sponsor costs exponentially more to register and keep alive. Like an opal valuable only because it is scarce, a single honest identity stays cheap, while a farm of thousands becomes ruinous. Honest newcomers still find a haven in the low first-identity price, but an attacker in the umber shadows of fake accounts pays a rising toll for every mask added, so flooding the network stops paying for itself.
